LESSON: IMITATION

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.1: Imitation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Imitation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: how, when and to?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Imitation

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Imitation

Teach
• Focus skill: respond confidently to sister, brother ), in pairs, small communication in different groups and whole class. contexts  The learners role play various.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Imitation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Imitation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how, when and to?
2. why people communicate 2) When do you speak to communication in different  Learners listen to and practice them?
3. Why do you speak to b) use appropriate vocabulary to  Learners simulate communication them?
4. how are you?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
